messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: A higher Geriatric Depression Scale score was significantly associated with vitamin D deficiency in frail older hospitalized patients.
Sentence: "In a stepwise logistic regression analysis, only previous intake of vitamin D supplementation and high Geriatric Depression Scale score (GDS-15) were significantly associated with vitamin D deficiency."
Measured as: Geriatric Depression Scale score (GDS-15)
Population: 217 consecutively admitted frail older geriatric hospitalized patients, mean age 81.6 years, 70% female
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D measured at hospital admission; no intervention given
Comparator: Not applicable (observational association; vitamin D sufficient vs deficient patients)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 217
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A is a cross-sectional association of depressive symptoms with vitamin D deficiency in frail inpatients, while Study B is a single-arm before/after case series of a vitamin D+folate+B12 combination in Parkinson's patients; the results point different ways chiefly because of design and exposure/intervention.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","intervention","outcome_measure"],"detail":"design: cross-sectional observational association (n=217) vs uncontrolled single-arm case series with combination supplement (n not reported)"}
